command: cargo build (plain rustc 1.95.0) on a crate with #[logic] items
symptom: rustc parses the body of a #[proc_macro_attribute]-annotated item as Rust even when the macro erases the item, so pearlite-only syntax (the @ snapshot operator) inside a #[logic] body breaks plain `cargo build` with a parse error, despite the dummy logic macro deleting the item. Reproduced with a 5-line proc macro that returns TokenStream::new(): `#[erase] pub fn probe(a: u32) -> u32 { a@ + 1 }` fails with 'expected one of `.`, `;`, `?`, `}`, or an operator, found `@`'. The creusot-std dummy logic macro returns TS1::new() (erases), so the item vanishes from the expanded code, but the parse error fires first. The sanctioned workaround is the pearlite! { ... } macro: the macro call itself is valid Rust (the @ inside is only tokenized), and under cfg(creusot) the real logic macro parses the body with pearlite-syn, which handles pearlite! natively (no import needed). This cost real debugging time because the plain-build error points at the @ inside a logic body, which looks like it should be fine.

symptom: R1's 'absent from I' finding has no worker-reachable resolution path once the C_static extractor CAN resolve a call. Resolving a possible-dispatch call site by spelling it as an associated-path call (Year::ok(&self.year) rather than self.year.ok()) turns it into a definite-direct-call, and R1 then REQUIRES it to be a declared interaction -- 'a definite direct call across concepts must be a declared interaction (its eligibility cannot even be computed while it has no edge_class)' -- at error severity. The only place an interaction can live is <crate_dir>/specs/_interactions/, which this project's descriptor lists in write_set.protected_roots ('rust/*/specs/**'), i.e. the agent is forbidden to write there; and even if it were written, an interaction is a normative artifact whose own review block, ci/results/review_log.jsonl entry, ci/results/human_rulings.jsonl ruling and specs/_promotions receipt all come from `approve` / `record-ruling` / `accept-promotion`, all human checkpoints the skill forbids an agent from running. Net effect: resolving the unresolved-call risk tier trades 6 medium human-decision-pending findings for N high R1 drift findings, and the pilot is then strictly worse off on exit codes with no legal move to close the new ones. The pre-existing I-year-month-day-last-to-year-month-day-last-new.json is lifecycle 'validated', not 'promoted', confirming that a hand-authored interaction never becomes normative without the approval path.

command: python3 tools/ligature/ligature.pyz report feature-ledger ; python3 tools/ligature/ligature.pyz gate-g14
symptom: Two Stage 8C commands write the same canonical path with incompatible schemas, so running the pipeline in its documented order silently destroys the evidence the closure gate reads. `report feature-ledger` writes a projection {features: [], generated_from: {...}, schema_version} to ci/results/feature_ledger.json; `record-assurance` writes an assurance report {obligation_records: [...5...], work_package: WP-DATE-CREUSOT, schema_version} to the SAME path, because the work-package manifest's report.emit names it. gate-g14 reads that path. On a tree where record-assurance has just populated it, gate-g14 exits 0 with 'OK: 1 cluster(s) close under their declared profile'; after a single `report feature-ledger` the identical tree gives gate-g14 exit 1 with six new errors: 'assurance report ci/results/feature_ledger.json is not schema-valid: 'work_package' is a required property', one 'recorded no achieved assurance' error per manifest obligation (Weekday.C1/C2/C3, YearMonthDay.C2, YearMonthDayLast.C1), and generic_callees flipping from 'VERIFIED from artifact data' to 'cannot verify it: no achieved assurance record at all for WP-DATE-CREUSOT'. This issue hit it for real: running the four Stage 8C report commands before the gates broke gate-g14 in the live pilot root, and only `record-assurance` re-run restored it (byte-identical, md5 463583d9eda1ed0292800703bf2835cf). The trap is silent in the failure direction: `report feature-ledger` still prints 'wrote ci/results/feature_ledger.json' and exits 0. `record-assurance` is the only one that warns, and its warning is easy to miss because it names the collision without making it an error.
repro_cmd: cd date-creusot && md5sum ci/results/feature_ledger.json && python3 tools/ligature/ligature.pyz report feature-ledger && md5sum ci/results/feature_ledger.json && python3 tools/ligature/ligature.pyz gate-g14
expected: The generated feature-ledger projection and the work package's assurance report are distinct artifacts at distinct paths, so regenerating one cannot invalidate the other; or `report feature-ledger` refuses to overwrite a path that holds an assurance report (or vice versa) instead of doing it silently at exit 0.
actual: `report feature-ledger` overwrites the assurance report at exit 0 with no warning, and gate-g14 then reports the whole cluster BLOCKED on 6 errors that were not true one command earlier. Confirmed on a clean rsync copy of this pilot: md5 463583d9eda1ed0292800703bf2835cf -> c8571e0944ad0eaefb60adf3a194bbea, gate-g14 0 -> 1, and the reverse is exactly recoverable by re-running record-assurance. Not a correctness bug in gate-g14 -- it is right to reject a schema-invalid report -- but an unrecoverable-by-default ordering trap in the Stage 8C command set. Extends date-ligature-047, which recorded the same collision from the record-assurance side and is now only half a picture: v1.1 DID fix the record-loss half ('preserved 4 existing obligation record(s) this run did not record') but the path collision itself is unchanged.
workaround: Run `report feature-ledger` BEFORE `record-assurance`, never after, and if gate-g14 reports 'is not schema-valid: work_package is a required property' or 'recorded no achieved assurance', re-run record-assurance with all five --proof flags before concluding anything about the closure. The full five-flag command is in this pilot's README under 'Current closure state'. The proper fix (pointing manifest.report.emit at a separate path) is not reachable by a worker -- see date-ligature-052.
revisit_trigger: Every issue that runs the Stage 8C report set: #18 here, and the P2/P3 equivalents. Also re-run on any ligature release; and it should be quoted in the Stage 8C runbook for P2 and P3 so neither pilot loses an hour to it.

The real side condition is valid_era_day(yoe, doy), i.e. '(yoe, doy) is a real day of era-year yoe'; an exhaustive 146400-pair brute force confirms valid_era_day selects EXACTLY the 146097 pairs on which the recovery inverts, so the precondition is tight rather than merely sufficient. (3) Two of the three nested-division identities one is tempted to state first are FALSE for C-truncating division and had to be restated: doe/36524 == (doe/1460)/25 fails at doe = 36500, and (x - 400*e) % m == x % m fails whenever the shift changes the sign (Why3's mod truncates towards zero), so the era-shift facts are needed as divisibility facts (div_4/100/400_era_shift), not remainder facts.
